interventions.step: Verify the production build in a browser
interventions.action: Installed playwright-core in work/.scratch/pw and drove the installed Google Chrome against `next start`. It checked dark and light at 320, 375 and 1280 px for sideways scrolling, computed --ult-color-accent, color-scheme and button colors. It also exercised list selection, the empty-name error, the Select opening from the keyboard, Escape and focus return, a new item, a donation to an existing item, and an explicit data-theme="light".
interventions.reason: The guidance says to check the root, a control and an open popup in production in both modes, but it names no tool for that, and init runs no browser checks.

decisions.choice: Accept the fallback font stack and do not load Figtree or IBM Plex Mono
decisions.why: The guidance says to load each face or accept the fallback, and leaves the choice open. Loading from Google would add an outside network fetch at build time, which this run's single-public-host limit argues against. The screen renders in the system UI font.

decisions.choice: Category uses the portalled Ultima Select, not a form inside a Dialog
options: Open the donation form in a Dialog
decisions.why: The brief accepts either. On a phone, an inline form with a Select avoids stacking a modal over the stock list, and the Select gets keyboard open, Escape close and focus return from Base UI. Dialog is installed by init but this screen does not use it.

decisions.choice: Ran the optional agent setup: `git init` in ./larder, then `ultima install --harness claude`
options: Install for codex, cursor or copilot
decisions.why: The init report lists this step as optional. Doing it adds .claude/skills/ultima-design/SKILL.md and a post-edit check hook to the project, which gave me the installed skill as a guidance source while building.

review.reviewer: Claude on mbp1, #774: transcript, request log, notes and production report
review.rule: An intervention is an action on the project or tooling that the guidance or CLI output did not print or link. A decision is an unresolved Ultima setup, theme or styling choice that changed the output. Product choices and documented alternatives do not count. Browser checks of the consumer application follow the guidance; rendering documentation to retrieve guidance or source would count.
review.notes: The agent fetched llms.txt, the install, update, build-a-screen, support and Recipes guides, and the projects, list-detail, interaction-states and product-tokens lessons over HTTP. It did not render documentation, decode a data link, extract a bundle, read CRM 01's registry source or reference the live host or another checkout. Both /r/theme.json requests came from the printed `shadcn add`. It read the printed `init --help`, ran init through --plan and --apply, installed the theme with the printed shadcn@4.21.4 command, imported ../../ultima-theme.css after ./ultima.css in src/app/layout.tsx as printed, ran init's printed optional agent setup, and set up ESLint by the documented project-without-ESLint path. Judgment call, recorded here: step #20 is an inspection command (grep over badge.tsx, field.tsx and input.tsx). The agent prefixed it with a second copy of the component install it had just run at #19, with `--overwrite=false` added and the output discarded. It repeats a printed command, it wrote nothing (`ultima-design status` at #24 reports every item current), and it did nothing to make the app work, so it is not counted as an intervention. The agent's own notes call it a mistake. It keeps `minBlockSize: '100dvh'` and its track templates literal, uses the documented DESKTOP and WIDE breakpoints as named constants, and puts only `--app-size-content-max` in screen.stylex.ts (#845 and #856 hold). Deleting init's setup-check preview after replacing page.tsx follows the starter comment. The browser check follows the printed hand step; the agent stopped its own server. The self-reported decisions (font fallback, Select over Dialog, agent setup) are documented options or product choices. check, doctor, StyleX lint (0 errors), the raw-paint scan and all four external production cases passed. No operator edited the app.
